data.title: Why Lululemon Stock Is Getting Battered Today, and Why Morgan Stanley Sees More Pain Ahead
data.description:
Lululemon Athletica (NASDAQ:LULU) is having a rough end to the week. Shares are plunging in Friday's session, down by 19% as of writing, after the athleisure company delivered another disappointing update, cutting its full-year sales outlook for the second time this year as weakness in China and growing competition in the U.S. continue to weigh on the business. The previous guidance reduction came in June, alongside the company's first-quarter results.

The latest numbers suggest the recovery will take longer than investors had hoped. Lululemon now expects full-year sales of $10.35 billion to $10.50 billion, representing a 5% to 7% decline and a major reduction from its prior forecast of $11.0 billion to $11.50 billion. The $10.425 billion midpoint is also well below Wall Street's forecast of $11.03 billion.

The earnings outlook has deteriorated just as sharply. Full-year adjusted earnings are now projected at $9.48 to $9.73 per share, compared with the previous forecast of $10.95 to $11.15 and analysts' $10.93 estimate.

Things look even worse in the near term. Lululemon expects current-quarter sales to fall 10% to 11%, reaching $2.29 billion to $2.32 billion vs. expectations of $2.53 billion. Adjusted earnings are forecast at just $0.93 to $0.98 per share, dramatically below the $2.41 consensus estimate.

The guidance cut follows a weak second quarter. Revenue fell by 4%, while comparable sales dropped 9%. The Americas were particularly problematic, with comparable sales down 12%, worse than the 10% decline analysts had expected. International comparable sales fell 3%, despite expectations for an increase of 8.61%. In Mainland China, comparable-store sales plunged 8%.

The stock is now down by 52% on a year-to-date basis, which begs the question: is it time to buy the dip? Not according to Morgan Stanley analyst Alex Straton. "The outsized guidance cut lowered the bar meaningfully, but we don't think the reset is done. Recent trends increase our conviction that new mgmt. will adopt a 'shrink to grow' strategy, which we think will drive another leg of negative EPS revisions."

Lululemon has already outlined several measures aimed at fixing the business, including reducing its product lineup, speeding up the supply chain, increasing marketing and optimizing its store base. Management is now adding tighter cost controls and a more cautious approach to store expansion, lowering its full-year opening target to 35 from 40.

Straton views those changes as constructive, particularly the greater focus on brand-building, social media and community engagement. However, she expects incoming CEO Heidi O'Neill, who takes over on September 8, to make a "broader set of strategic adjustments."

Straton estimates that a roughly 20% reduction to 2027 earnings could push consensus expectations toward $9 per share. That remains above her updated $8 forecast and the $6 estimate held by some of the more bearish analysts. "Thus," says Straton, "we stay braced for negative EPS revisions & further valuation de-rating, keeping our Underweight (i.e., Sell) thesis intact."

Straton has now lowered her price target from $93 to $83, implying further downside of 16.5% over the coming months. (To watch Straton's track record, click here)

Two other analysts join Straton in the bear camp, although an additional 20 Holds all add up to a Hold consensus rating. Going by the $101.79 average price target, the shares will stay rangebound for the time being. (See LULU stock forecast)

data.title: Snowflake vs. Oracle: Bernstein Says One Enterprise AI Stock Is Undervalued, While the Other Faces Uncertainty
data.description:
Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW) and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) both sit at the heart of the enterprise data boom, but they are benefiting from it in different ways. Oracle has been turning its long-established database business into a much broader cloud and AI infrastructure operation, while Snowflake has built its business around helping companies make better use of the vast amounts of data they generate. That puts both companies in a position to benefit from the rapid adoption of AI, which is driving demand not only for computing power but also for the data infrastructure needed to train and run AI applications.

Their stocks, however, are telling very different stories right now. Oracle has spent much of the year under pressure (down by 20% year-to-date), with shares still well below last year's record high as investors grapple with the enormous cost of its AI infrastructure ambitions.

Snowflake, by contrast, has also been under pressure earlier this year over fears AI will make software companies obsolete. But the company has just delivered a major earnings-fueled breakout, with shares surging more than 16% on Thursday after it beat Wall Street's expectations and raised its full-year outlook, renewing investor confidence in its AI strategy.

Promotion

200% short exposure to ORCL with ORCZ

Bernstein analyst Mark Moerdler views the results as an impressive showing from the data warehouse company. Expectations were already elevated heading into the report, with investors looking for evidence of a meaningful pickup in revenue growth. Moerdler said Snowflake not only met those heightened expectations but delivered the additional catalyst needed to propel the stock higher.

The company's product revenue growth accelerated to 37% from 34% in the prior quarter, coming in 4.5% ahead of consensus expectations. Snowflake also increased its FY27 product revenue growth forecast by five percentage points, taking it to 36% and pointing to a significant step-up in growth compared with last year.

According to management, the strength extended across the customer base rather than being concentrated in a particular group of clients. Moerdler noted that AI was an important contributor, while broader AI adoption was also creating tailwinds for Snowflake's core business.

Snowflake is also seeing direct benefits from its AI offerings, particularly CoWork, previously known as Snowflake Intelligence, which enables data analysis and actions, and CoCo, formerly Cortex Codex, which is aimed at coding and development.

However, Moerdler sees a more difficult question emerging over the longer term. As important corporate data shifts into the cloud and SaaS providers and hyperscalers build out their own AI capabilities, it remains uncertain whether AI functionality will eventually move back into these core enterprise systems. While there is not enough evidence to answer that question yet, Moerdler said Snowflake's progress to date has been impressive.

But that is not enough to support the bull case. "While we are encouraged by the innovation and execution focus under the new CEO, we remain concerned about longer-term competition with hyperscalers, AI labs and big SaaS vendors," the 5-star analyst said. "At this valuation, we choose to stay on the sidelines."

As such, Moerdler rates the stock as Market-Perform. Moerdler's $377 price target implies shares will gain a modest 6% over the next year. (To watch Moerdler's track record, click here)

Attention now turns to Oracle, which is set to release its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results next Thursday, Sept. 10. Moerdler said the stock remains an "extremely controversial and volatile" name, with the debate largely revolving around its push into AI datacenters. In particular, investors are concerned about the profitability and financial stability of the massive buildout, as well as Oracle's ability to meet its significant cash needs and long-term contractual commitments.

However, Oracle's revenue growth has been "steadily improving," helped by Cloud revenue outpacing the company's other businesses. That performance has been supported by OCI Gen II, including cloud database and AI, as well as Strategic Back Office offerings such as ERP and HCM.

Moerdler expects that momentum to carry into FY27, with the Cloud business serving as the primary engine of faster growth. In his view, Oracle's current investment cycle could ultimately produce not only stronger revenue and earnings but also the technological capabilities and market credibility required to capture revenue from sovereign Cloud AI. "We believe that the company is nearing the end of its need for additional cash. The value being created is substantial and not included in the valuation," the analyst commented.

To this end, Moerdler reiterated an Outperform (i.e., Buy) rating, backed by a $325 price target. Should the figure be met, investors will be pocketing returns of 111% one year from now.

Elsewhere on the Street, these stocks get plenty of support, with both claiming Strong Buy consensus ratings. With a $432.03 average price target, SNOW stock is expected to appreciate by 21% over the 12-month timeframe. ORCL shares are expected to climb by 65%, considering its average target lands at $254.68. (See SNOW stock forecast or ORCL stock forecast)

data.title: Trump Threatens to End Trade With Deficit Countries Unless Fed Slashes Rates
data.description:
President Trump threatened on Friday to eliminate trade with countries which the U.S. carries a deficit unless the Fed lowers interest rates. The U.S. currently has a trade deficit with several key trading partners, including China, Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Germany.

"LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT," Trump said in a Truth Social post. "IT'S BETTER THAN TARIFFS!" he added.

Strong Payrolls Lift Fed Rate Hike Expectations

Trump's statement came after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced that nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, well above expectations of 55,000. In addition, the unemployment rate remained unchanged from the prior month at 4.1%. However, rate hike expectations rose following the data, as a stronger labor market gives the Fed flexibility to raise rates. That comes as inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for 65 consecutive months.

data.title: When Will LULU Stock Hit Bottom? Asks Wells Fargo; Cuts Price Target on Weak Results
data.description:
Lululemon Athletica (LULU) stock plunged 20% in premarket trading after the athletic-apparel company reported weak second-quarter results and lowered its full-year outlook. With demand weakening and margins under pressure, Wells Fargo analyst Ike Boruchow is asking, "Where's the bottom?"

Boruchow cut his price target on LULU to $95 from $105, while maintaining a Hold rating. The new target implies nearly 22% downside from Thursday's closing price of $121.77. The premarket sell-off also pushed LULU stock to an 8-year low.

Lululemon reported a 4% year-over-year decline in second-quarter revenue to $2.4 billion, missing analysts' estimate of $2.46 billion. Comparable sales fell 9%, while sales in the Americas, the company's largest market, declined 8%.

Why Is Wells Fargo Worried About LULU Stock?

According to Boruchow, investors are now facing several challenges at the same time.

First, demand appears to be worsening. Lululemon has been struggling to maintain momentum in its core Americas business, with competition from brands such as Alo and Vuori adding pressure.

Second, weaker sales are creating fixed-cost deleverage. This means that when revenue falls, costs such as stores, employees and other fixed expenses do not decline at the same pace. As a result, profits can fall much faster than sales.

Third, Lululemon continues to rely on markdowns to move merchandise. Higher discounts can help clear inventory, but they also put pressure on profit margins.

Lululemon also received $134.5 million in tariff refunds and interest, adding $0.86 to quarterly EPS and boosting its gross margin by 5.6 percentage points. However, this benefit may not continue next year.

Could LULU Earnings Fall Below $6?

Boruchow's sees LULU's 2027 EPS falling to around $6.00 based on the current challenges, representing less than half of the earnings generated in the previous year.

The analyst believes that If Lululemon's earnings continue to fall, investors may be less willing to pay a premium for the stock. Lululemon has traditionally traded at a higher valuation because of its strong brand value, growth, and healthy profit margins.

New CEO Could Be the Biggest Catalyst

Lululemon's new CEO, former Nike (NKE) executive Heidi O'Neill, will take over on September 8 and focus on reviving North American sales and the brand. However, Boruchow does not expect investors to get immediate clarity.

He noted that the timeline for hearing from new management on its forward strategy could extend into next year. With limited visibility into the turnaround plan, he said he does not see a "credible Bull case for shares today."

Is Now a Good Time to Buy LULU Stock?

On TipRanks, LULU has a Hold consensus rating based on zero Buys, 19 Holds, and three Sell ratings. The average Lululemon Athletica price target of $102.67 implies 15.7% downside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, LULU shares have dropped 41.4%.

data.title: "Sell the News," Says GLJ Research Analyst as Tesla Stock Sinks After Cybercab Launch Backfires
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) shares are down over 6% on Friday after the EV giant's Cybercab robotaxi launch failed to meet investor expectations and immediately drew a federal safety audit. Following the event, GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson reiterated his Sell rating and $24.86 price target. Thus, the analyst concluded that the event was a "sell‑the‑news" moment, meaning it did not deliver enough to justify Tesla's recent run‑up.

On the regulatory front, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has opened a formal audit into nearly 1,000 Cybercabs. Since the two-seater vehicle lacks a steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors, it does not meet federal safety standards.

Here's Why the Analyst Is Disappointed With the Event

Johnson noted that Tesla offered no rollout target, no pricing, no consumer order option, no livestream, and no appearance from CEO Elon Musk. Instead, Tesla invited a group of friendly creators, who took short rides in a two‑seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, then posted about it online.

Promotion

According to state filings, only 45 Cybercabs were registered with the Texas DMV as of Wednesday, a number far below what bullish expectations had outlined. It must be noted that Alphabet's (GOOGL) Waymo already runs nearly 1,000 autonomous vehicles in the state, which makes Tesla's scale look very small in comparison.

Johnson argued that while engineering progress is real, the stock is priced for a full robotaxi network rather than a few cars in one city. He noted the disappointment came as Tesla's most supportive analysts had set a low bar for success and Tesla still came in below it.

For instance, Morgan Stanley had said 25-50 Cybercabs across Texas would likely push the stock higher, and that paid, unsupervised rides across multiple cities would represent a bullish outcome. Instead, Tesla showed one city, an unknown subset of 45 cars, and an app that did not let users request a ride as of Thursday night.

data.title: Micron Stock Faces Peak Risk by Late 2028 as Nvidia Budgets $267 Billion Memory Spend Through 2030
data.description:
Micron stock (MU) is facing a key risk. The risk is that its biggest buyer, Nvidia (NVDA), has only booked orders through 2030. Micron builds fast memory chips that pair with Nvidia processors to power AI models. Huge demand for these chips helped Micron stock surge 697% over the past year. However, if Nvidia buys fewer chips later, Micron stock's price run could end early.

Memory chip sales usually move in big ups and downs. While Micron stock trades near high levels, Nvidia's newest spending table gives investors a clear look at when this easy profit era might slow down.

Nvidia Budgets $267 Billion Memory Spend Through Fiscal 2030

Nvidia reported that its future order commitments grew from $119 billion to $279 billion, with most of that money going to memory chip makers like Micron, SK Hynix (SKHY), and Samsung (SSNLF).

Promotion

Nvidia plans to spend $92 billion for the rest of Fiscal 2027, $87 billion in Fiscal 2028, and $88 billion in Fiscal 2029. This sets aside $267 billion for memory and supplies through January 2030. But in Fiscal 2030, Nvidia's booked orders fall to just $6 billion. Since memory chips are in short supply today, chipmakers make buyers sign multi-year deals, but Nvidia has not signed deals at today's high prices past 2029.

Should Micron Stock Investors Be Cautious?

Yes. Caution is advised. Nvidia's drop in booked orders from $88 billion down to $6 billion sets a trap for Micron stock investors. Micron will still ship memory chips through 2029 to fill older orders, which will keep its short-term sales reports looking strong.

However, stock markets like to look ahead. While Micron stock could keep rising through 2027 and 2028 on current sales, investors will not wait until 2030 to sell. If Nvidia does not sign new high-priced memory deals, markets could re-rate Micron stock between December 2028 and January 2029. This could lead to a price drop in MU stock.

Is Micron a Good Stock to Buy?

Turning to the Street, Micron stock carries a Strong Buy consensus based on 31 Buys and one Hold rating assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month MU stock price target is $1,554.67, which implies over 55.67% upside from the current price. (See MU stock forecast)

data.title: American Outdoor Brands Stock (AOUT) Surges More than 34% on Strong Q2 Growth
data.description:
American Outdoor Brands (AOUT) stock was up 34.67% on Friday after the outdoor gear and accessories company reported a strong start to fiscal 2027, with first-quarter revenue rising 25.4% to $37.3 million. The year-ago quarter had about $6 million in orders pulled forward by retailers, so sales rose 4.3% after removing that impact. Growth was broad across both Outdoor Lifestyle and Shooting Sports, as point-of-sale sales rose 6% in Outdoor Lifestyle and 3% in Shooting Sports.

Profit also improved as new products helped lift margins. Gross margin rose 630 basis points to 53.0%. GAAP net loss fell to $1.5 million from $6.8 million a year ago. On an adjusted basis, the company swung to $415,000 in net income from a $3.3 million loss. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.2 million from a $3.1 million loss. The company ended the quarter with $33.3 million in cash and no debt.

American Outdoor Brands noted that new products made up more than 36% of sales in the quarter. Caldwell's ClayCopter line saw strong demand and won the 2026 Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year award. Bubba also added new products, including its Pro Series Gen 2 Electric Fillet Knife. The company also launched Scoretracker Live with Major League Fishing, adding a digital service to Bubba's fishing gear. "We believe this approach has the potential to extend to other brands in our portfolio over time," said Brian Murphy, president and CEO of American Outdoor Brands.
